assets.title: Inspect the analytics data footprint
assets.content:
Subject: Inspect the analytics data footprint
Preview text: See the fields Simple Analytics processes before evaluating it for a client site.

See what client-site analytics actually processes

Hi there,

Before evaluating analytics for a client site, you can review the exact data footprint the service is designed to use.

Simple Analytics is cookie-free website analytics. It uses no persistent identifiers, stores no IP addresses—they are discarded immediately—and does not link its metrics to identifiable users.

Its public data-processing page lists the scope: Page URL, referrer, UTM parameters, time zone, and device and browser type. You can inspect these fields without signing up or installing anything.

This gives you a concrete model to review and explain, rather than a general privacy claim. Compare the documented fields with each client’s requirements, then decide whether Simple Analytics is suitable for an evaluation on their site.

Review the data scope → https://www.simpleanalytics.com/data-processing-agreement

- Simple Analytics

asset_metadata.single_idea: Simple Analytics is worth considering as a client-site analytics default because its privacy proposition rests on inspectable collection choices: no cookies, no stored IP addresses, and a limited documented data scope that is not linked to identifiable users.

selected_brief.selection_reason: The audience research shows direct skepticism about whether privacy-friendly analytics claims reflect the actual collection mechanism. Simple Analytics can answer that question with documented technical specifics that are relevant when recommending an analytics stack to clients.

value_case.reader_benefit: For suitable client sites, the developer can provide website-traffic analytics with a data footprint that is concrete enough to review and explain: no cookies, no stored IP addresses, and a documented set of processed website and device fields that are not linked to identifiable users.
value_case.mechanism: Simple Analytics operates without cookies, discards IP addresses immediately rather than storing them, and documents processing Page URL, Referrer, UTM parameters, Time zone, and Device and browser type without linking those metrics to identifiable users.
decision_conditions: These facts describe Simple Analytics' documented technical behavior; they do not establish a universal legal conclusion for every client configuration or jurisdiction.
Suitability still needs to be checked against each client's requirements.

claim_conditions: Frame the application to client sites conditionally because no recipient or company has been qualified.
Keep legal applicability separate from the documented collection and storage design.
Add each website and use the technology-detected HTML code or another documented platform or framework installation option.

The documented per-site installation and privacy behavior support an exploratory product evaluation across client builds, but R15 describes the additional-website rule in a subdomain context and does not establish the Self-serve site cap or aggregate portfolio cost; the research also does not verify firsthand agency demand or recipient qualification.
These sources document Simple Analytics' own behavior and stated GDPR basis; they do not establish a universal legal conclusion for every client configuration or jurisdiction.
selected_brief.target_audience: Agency or freelance developer choosing the analytics stack for client sites
selected_brief.job: Give the reader a concrete technical reason to consider Simple Analytics and get them to inspect its documented data scope before deciding whether to evaluate it on a client site.
selected_brief.single_idea: Simple Analytics is worth considering as a client-site analytics default because its privacy proposition rests on inspectable collection choices: no cookies, no stored IP addresses, and a limited documented data scope that is not linked to identifiable users.
selected_brief.felt_need: Whether adopting a cookie-free or 'privacy-friendly' analytics tool actually removes the need for a cookie consent banner is directly disputed among developers, with claims that named alternatives (Fathom, Plausible) still use techniques that may require consent, and skepticism that first-party analytics cookies qualify as 'strictly necessary.'
selected_brief.mechanism: Simple Analytics documents that it uses no cookies, discards IP addresses immediately, and processes a defined set of website and device fields without linking them to identifiable users.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: A developer considering a repeatable default may instead respond to a practical way to explore the product and see installation guidance for a representative site.

value_case.reader_benefit: The developer can explore Simple Analytics on a representative site and see installation guidance selected for that site's detected technology before considering broader use across client builds.
value_case.mechanism: The onboarding flow scans the website and provides technology-dependent HTML code or another documented platform or framework installation option; the self-serve trial provides 14 days to explore Simple Analytics independently.
decision_conditions: Installation is performed per site and exact code placement can depend on the website.
The self-guided trial is distinct from the assisted 30-day GA4 proof of concept.

claim_conditions: Present this as an evaluation on a representative site, not proof of compatibility or economics across an entire client portfolio.
Add each website and use the technology-detected HTML code or another documented platform or framework installation option.

The documented per-site installation and privacy behavior support an exploratory product evaluation across client builds, but R15 describes the additional-website rule in a subdomain context and does not establish the Self-serve site cap or aggregate portfolio cost; the research also does not verify firsthand agency demand or recipient qualification.
alternative_arguments.single_idea: A 14-day self-guided trial lets a developer explore Simple Analytics while its onboarding flow supplies installation guidance based on the technology detected on the chosen site.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: After a website is added, Simple Analytics scans it and offers technology-dependent install code or another documented platform or framework option; the 14-day trial is self-guided.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: evaluating another analytics option may appear to require committing to a generic installation path. After: one representative site can be explored through a self-guided trial with technology-dependent installation guidance.
must_not_say: Do not promise one universal installation step or instant setup.
Do not claim compatibility with every client platform or framework.
Do not imply that the trial includes the assisted 30-day GA4 comparison.
Do not claim that testing one site proves suitability, cost, or scalability across a client portfolio.

Keep the connection route attached to its cited source. A native or prebuilt integration and a custom HTTP/webhook endpoint are separate setup paths unless the source explicitly equates them. A platform name alone establishes neither manual endpoint configuration nor a no-setup connector. Keep unknown setup requirements unknown; do not mix the steps or benefits of those paths.
alternative_arguments.objection: Will the installation path fit the kind of site I would use it on?
alternative_arguments.call_to_action: Start the 14-day self-guided trial on a representative site.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether the installation flow and product are suitable for a practical evaluation on that type of client build.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The signup path provides access to the self-guided trial, where the reader can explore Simple Analytics and use the technology-dependent onboarding flow for a chosen website.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: One trial installation does not establish compatibility, commercial fit, or rollout effort across every client site.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Signal a practical, site-specific evaluation rather than making a broad ease-of-migration promise.

selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: privacy-friendly analytics may sound like an unverified category claim. After: Simple Analytics offers a documented collection and storage model the reader can inspect before deciding whether to test it.
must_not_say: Do not state that Simple Analytics universally removes consent-banner, contract, DPA, or regulatory obligations for every client or jurisdiction.
Do not present the vendor's legal interpretation as an authoritative legal conclusion.
Do not claim that competitors collect fingerprints, store IP addresses, or require consent.
Do not promise improved traffic counts, more complete data, revenue gains, or a customer outcome.
Do not claim setup is instant, universal, or effortless across client sites.
Do not make portfolio pricing or the number of websites covered by a plan part of this argument.
Do not add EU hosting, encryption, scroll depth, time-on-page, GA4 comparisons, customer logos, or other features that dilute the single data-design argument.
selected_brief.objection: Privacy-friendly analytics claims are disputed; what does this product actually collect and store?
selected_brief.tone: Matter-of-fact, technically concrete, and reassuring without sounding legalistic or defensive.
selected_brief.next_step_decision: Decide whether Simple Analytics' documented data design is suitable enough for a client-site evaluation.
selected_brief.next_step_value: The public data-processing documentation shows the stated field scope and explains that those metrics are not linked to identifiable users.
selected_brief.next_step_limit: The page documents Simple Analytics' own processing model; it does not determine legal applicability for every client configuration or jurisdiction.
selected_brief.subject_strategy: Earn the open by pointing to the inspectable data footprint behind the privacy claim, not by promising compliance or criticizing another analytics tool.

brief.reader:
Selected audience: Agency or freelance developer choosing the analytics stack for client sites.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (inferred; check applicability): The corpus contains public developer discussion (two Hacker News threads) about whether websites need cookie consent banners and about named analytics tools (Google Analytics, Fathom, Plausible, SimpleAnalytics), but no quote in either thread identifies the speaker as an agency or freelance developer building or maintaining multiple client websites, or as selecting an analytics default on behalf of clients. The audience's defining workflow (choosing a repeatable analytics default across client builds to avoid consent-banner/DPA friction) is not directly evidenced here; only general developer debate about consent and analytics tool choice is present.
brief.reader_segment: Agency or freelance developer choosing the analytics stack for client sites
brief.promise: Simple Analytics gives developers a concrete, inspectable analytics data model they can assess for client sites without relying on a generic privacy-friendly label.
brief.orientation: Simple Analytics is a cookie-free website analytics option for agencies and freelance developers evaluating a repeatable default across client sites, with per-site installation and documented privacy conditions.
brief.arc: In this single email, move the reader from skepticism about privacy-friendly analytics claims to interest in Simple Analytics because its collection and storage choices are documented and can be inspected before adoption.
brief.sequence_rationale: The single slot leads with the strongest supported fit for this solution-aware audience: the concrete data design behind the privacy proposition. The public documentation is a lower-friction next step than registration because it lets the reader assess the relevant fields and boundaries before deciding whether installation is worthwhile. A self-guided installation evaluation is retained as a complete alternative proposition, but it asks for more commitment and does not answer the reader's first technical eligibility question as directly. No customer outcome or blanket legal exemption is needed to make the primary case. A readable copy of the currently unavailable homepage source, or verification of its missing details, would most change this campaign.

emails.selection_reason: The audience research shows direct skepticism about whether privacy-friendly analytics claims reflect the actual collection mechanism. Simple Analytics can answer that question with documented technical specifics that are relevant when recommending an analytics stack to clients.

value_case.reader_benefit: For suitable client sites, the developer can provide website-traffic analytics with a data footprint that is concrete enough to review and explain: no cookies, no stored IP addresses, and a documented set of processed website and device fields that are not linked to identifiable users.
value_case.mechanism: Simple Analytics operates without cookies, discards IP addresses immediately rather than storing them, and documents processing Page URL, Referrer, UTM parameters, Time zone, and Device and browser type without linking those metrics to identifiable users.
decision_conditions: These facts describe Simple Analytics' documented technical behavior; they do not establish a universal legal conclusion for every client configuration or jurisdiction.
Suitability still needs to be checked against each client's requirements.

claim_conditions: Frame the application to client sites conditionally because no recipient or company has been qualified.
Keep legal applicability separate from the documented collection and storage design.

emails.target_audience: Agency or freelance developer choosing the analytics stack for client sites
emails.job: Give the reader a concrete technical reason to consider Simple Analytics and get them to inspect its documented data scope before deciding whether to evaluate it on a client site.
emails.single_idea: Simple Analytics is worth considering as a client-site analytics default because its privacy proposition rests on inspectable collection choices: no cookies, no stored IP addresses, and a limited documented data scope that is not linked to identifiable users.
emails.felt_need: Whether adopting a cookie-free or 'privacy-friendly' analytics tool actually removes the need for a cookie consent banner is directly disputed among developers, with claims that named alternatives (Fathom, Plausible) still use techniques that may require consent, and skepticism that first-party analytics cookies qualify as 'strictly necessary.'
emails.mechanism: Simple Analytics documents that it uses no cookies, discards IP addresses immediately, and processes a defined set of website and device fields without linking them to identifiable users.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: A developer considering a repeatable default may instead respond to a practical way to explore the product and see installation guidance for a representative site.

value_case.reader_benefit: The developer can explore Simple Analytics on a representative site and see installation guidance selected for that site's detected technology before considering broader use across client builds.
value_case.mechanism: The onboarding flow scans the website and provides technology-dependent HTML code or another documented platform or framework installation option; the self-serve trial provides 14 days to explore Simple Analytics independently.
decision_conditions: Installation is performed per site and exact code placement can depend on the website.
The self-guided trial is distinct from the assisted 30-day GA4 proof of concept.

claim_conditions: Present this as an evaluation on a representative site, not proof of compatibility or economics across an entire client portfolio.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: A 14-day self-guided trial lets a developer explore Simple Analytics while its onboarding flow supplies installation guidance based on the technology detected on the chosen site.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: After a website is added, Simple Analytics scans it and offers technology-dependent install code or another documented platform or framework option; the 14-day trial is self-guided.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: evaluating another analytics option may appear to require committing to a generic installation path. After: one representative site can be explored through a self-guided trial with technology-dependent installation guidance.
must_not_say: Do not promise one universal installation step or instant setup.
Do not claim compatibility with every client platform or framework.
Do not imply that the trial includes the assisted 30-day GA4 comparison.
Do not claim that testing one site proves suitability, cost, or scalability across a client portfolio.

Keep the connection route attached to its cited source. A native or prebuilt integration and a custom HTTP/webhook endpoint are separate setup paths unless the source explicitly equates them. A platform name alone establishes neither manual endpoint configuration nor a no-setup connector. Keep unknown setup requirements unknown; do not mix the steps or benefits of those paths.
alternative_arguments.objection: Will the installation path fit the kind of site I would use it on?
alternative_arguments.call_to_action: Start the 14-day self-guided trial on a representative site.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether the installation flow and product are suitable for a practical evaluation on that type of client build.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The signup path provides access to the self-guided trial, where the reader can explore Simple Analytics and use the technology-dependent onboarding flow for a chosen website.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: One trial installation does not establish compatibility, commercial fit, or rollout effort across every client site.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Signal a practical, site-specific evaluation rather than making a broad ease-of-migration promise.

emails.belief_shift: Before: privacy-friendly analytics may sound like an unverified category claim. After: Simple Analytics offers a documented collection and storage model the reader can inspect before deciding whether to test it.
must_not_say: Do not state that Simple Analytics universally removes consent-banner, contract, DPA, or regulatory obligations for every client or jurisdiction.
Do not present the vendor's legal interpretation as an authoritative legal conclusion.
Do not claim that competitors collect fingerprints, store IP addresses, or require consent.
Do not promise improved traffic counts, more complete data, revenue gains, or a customer outcome.
Do not claim setup is instant, universal, or effortless across client sites.
Do not make portfolio pricing or the number of websites covered by a plan part of this argument.
Do not add EU hosting, encryption, scroll depth, time-on-page, GA4 comparisons, customer logos, or other features that dilute the single data-design argument.
emails.objection: Privacy-friendly analytics claims are disputed; what does this product actually collect and store?
emails.tone: Matter-of-fact, technically concrete, and reassuring without sounding legalistic or defensive.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Simple Analytics' documented data design is suitable enough for a client-site evaluation.
emails.next_step_value: The public data-processing documentation shows the stated field scope and explains that those metrics are not linked to identifiable users.
emails.next_step_limit: The page documents Simple Analytics' own processing model; it does not determine legal applicability for every client configuration or jurisdiction.
emails.subject_strategy: Earn the open by pointing to the inspectable data footprint behind the privacy claim, not by promising compliance or criticizing another analytics tool.

brief.voice_notes: Use the company's short cause-and-effect rhythm. Avoid hype, urgency, superlatives, legal conclusions, and named-competitor attacks.

reasons: A licensed product bridge exists only for the qualified slice.
allowed_claims: Simple Analytics requires no cookies, no trackers, and no consent from visitors.
The Self-serve plan costs €20/month, estimated for about 100k monthly pageviews.
The Self-serve plan includes 1 user; each additional user costs +€20/month.
Simple Analytics offers a free 30-day proof of concept to test it on your own website, including help optimizing the setup for proxies and custom domains.
Website data is stored in the EU, with primary infrastructure in the Netherlands.
Data only goes to a provider outside the EU when the customer opts in to a feature that needs it, such as the AI assistant.
By default, Simple Analytics does not collect or store any data for visitors who have Do Not Track enabled.
Simple Analytics collects and stores how long a page is viewed, counting seconds only while the page is visible and not when it is hidden.
Simple Analytics collects and stores how far a visitor scrolls on a page, recorded in 5% increments.
All analytics data is processed in the Netherlands (EU-hosted).
No IP addresses are stored; they are discarded immediately.
Data is encrypted, and only Simple Analytics controls the decryption keys.
Simple Analytics is hosted on infrastructure from Worldstream and Leaseweb.
Simple Analytics does not process personal data, so a Data Processing Agreement is not required when using it.
Simple Analytics processes only Page URL, Referrer, UTM parameters, Time zone, and Device and browser type as its data scope.
The installation flow is technology-dependent: Simple Analytics scans each site and offers install code based on detected technologies rather than a single universal step.
Across Simple Analytics generally, additional websites/subdomains added to an account do not cost extra individually, but are capped by a plan-wide website limit.
recommendation.recommended_next_action: Draft only around the addressed needs and the dossier's scope limits. No companies have been qualified; verify recipient fit before outreach.
recommendation.override_risk: Generating outside the eligible slice risks writing to a structurally similar company whose actual need the product cannot support.
